rounds.text: Abril Paper Tech Ltd trades at an attractive valuation across multiple metrics, sitting at a price-to-book ratio of just 1.15x on a book value of ₹ 29.8 against a market price of ₹ 34.4 [E2]. This valuation is distinctly lower than the broader sector benchmark price-to-book ratio of 2.58x [E7]. Further supporting the undervalued thesis, a discounted cash flow model establishes an intrinsic value of ₹ 43 per share, providing a 19.1% margin of safety at the current price [E29, E30]. Additionally, the company's reverse discounted cash flow indicates that today's price implies an earnings growth rate of only 7.0%, which is conservative compared to the 10.0% assumed in the base case [E31]. Operational efficiency also shines through, with a return on assets of 6.15% that outperforms the sector benchmark of 4.68% [E8]. Conceded: the dividend yield stands at 0.00% [E4], and the stock currently languishes at just 28% of the way up its 52-week range [E5].

The bull leans heavily on a discounted cash flow intrinsic value of ₹ 43 and a 19.1% margin of safety [E29, E30], yet the screen engine explicitly flags this exact characteristic—trading below DCF value—as a primary bear signal warning of a trapped value asset [E41]. While the bull cites a price-to-book ratio of 1.15x against a sector benchmark of 2.58x [E2, E7] to claim undervaluation, the stock languishes at a mere 28% of its 52-week range [E5] and delivers a complete 0.00% dividend yield [E4], offering investors zero cash return while remaining stuck near its yearly lows. Conceded: the company prints a return on assets of 6.15% beating the sector's 4.68% [E8], and its reverse DCF implies a modest 7.0% growth expectation [E31]. However, that low implied growth and discounted multiple are entirely justified by a depressed market capitalization of ₹ 27.5 Cr [E3] and a sluggish momentum profile where the equity fails to attract capital despite optical multiple discounts.
